events.title: LXC released
events.summary: Daniel Lezcano published the first LXC commit on August 6, 2008 — Linux Containers using cgroups and namespaces for lightweight OS virtualization.
events.about: LXC wraps kernel isolation primitives into `lxc-create`, `lxc-start`, and templates for minimal root filesystems. It predated Docker but shared the same insight: package an app with its dependencies in an isolated environment without full hardware VMs. Docker initially built on LXC before switching to libcontainer — and LXC remains the foundation many container runtimes still depend on.

narrative.whyChosen: LXC was the first user-facing toolkit to operationalize Linux kernel containers.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved OS-level virtualization was practical years before Docker popularized containers for developers.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams needed denser isolation than chroot jails but lighter overhead than hypervisor VMs.
